articles.title: Traces on the Water
articles.ru: Traces on the Water — the First Novel of the World of Wells
aliases: first book of the World of Wells
articles.summary: Roman Surzhikov’s first novel about the World of Wells: a Catalian writer investigates a death and threats surrounding the heroes of a long-ago expedition, an enslaved Catalian digs a well in a Dangarian forest, and a Dangarian lieutenant tries to buy himself a miracle.
searchAliases: «Следы на воде» — первый роман мира колодцев

articles.title: Alvaro da Silva
articles.ru: Alvaro Flores da Silva
articles.summary: A writer from Laerta, a maestro of the esfera of Art, a main character and the narrator of the preface to Traces on the Water. Commissioned by Filippe di Berro to write a book about the heroes of the Solantan Expedition, he becomes involved in an investigation that leads him to the secret of Last Winter.

articles.title: Amir the Grey
articles.ru: Amir the Grey, “he who sees the depths,” magnus of the Order of Fishermen
articles.summary: Magnus of the Fishermen’s Guild (Order), the “third man in Dangar,” and Joriksen’s mentor. An old man with a golden clepsydra that slows time; he investigates the destruction of Dunkwald.
searchAliases: Амир Седой, «видящий глубину», магнус ордена рыбаков

articles.title: Balboa
articles.ru: Don Balboa, arms factory owner
articles.summary: An arms manufacturer of the esfera of Production whose guards and hired thugs from the esfera of Shadow beat dismissed obreros and provoked a city riot in Laerta; he does not appear in person in the novel.

articles.title: Beatriz
articles.ru: Beatriz Enhal, nicknamed Golden Quill
articles.summary: A red-haired student at the Academy of Arts, Alvaro’s pupil and assistant; she drives the fast steam carriage Esperanza and dreams of writing a great book.
searchAliases: Беатрис Энхаль, по прозвищу Золотое Перо

articles.title: Spadebeard
articles.ru: Spadebeard, a slave from Red’s dugout
articles.summary: A slave from Red’s first dugout with a ragged beard; later he digs a pit, plucking one beard hair to put into each shovelful of earth.
searchAliases: Борода Лопатой, раб из землянки Рэда

articles.title: Foreman
articles.ru: Foreman of the slaves' dugout (the twenty-ninth dugout, according to ch. 23)
articles.summary: The unnamed senior slave in the dugout where Red lives—a lazy tyrant to his neighbors, Red's enemy, and the man who buries him in the pit; in Dunkwald he becomes the “beast's” first victim.
searchAliases: Бригадир землянки рабов (по гл. 23 — двадцать девятой землянки)

articles.title: Brojenstoff
articles.ru: Brojenstoff, General of Infantry
articles.summary: A Dangarian general of infantry commanding the army that moved into Ollandia's northern “shepherd” provinces after the capture of Latsen. The narrator calls him the least capable of the three commanders; Deserey calls him a dim-witted career soldier.

articles.title: Gabriel Deserey
articles.ru: Gabriel Deserey, general
articles.summary: A Catalian general and one of the heroes of the Solantan Expedition; convinced that war with Dangar awaits his country, he tries to make Alvaro da Silva write a book that will frighten its readers.

articles.title: Diego Ingres
articles.ru: Diego Ingres
articles.summary: An alguacil at the Foucault Street station in the Arts district; he explains to Alvaro why a severed finger and a threatening note do not constitute a crime.

articles.title: Dietrich von Dort
articles.ru: Dietrich Wolfgang von Dort
articles.summary: A young Dangarian artillery lieutenant from the landless eagles and one of the novel’s three main characters; after winning a battle with a well’s “guidance,” he must find a way to regain his position and good name.

articles.title: Elsa von Walbrecht
articles.ru: Baroness Elsa von Walbrecht (“Frau Elsa”)
articles.summary: A wealthy baroness from Hofstadt, owner of the schönbrun known as the Beautiful Well, and hostess of annual fishing parties. Close to Master Joriksen, she acts as Olkha’s patron and hosts Prince Lenz in her home.

articles.title: Emil Diale
articles.ru: Emil Diale, Doctor Juanes’s butler
articles.summary: Doctor Juanes’s butler, who unwittingly caused his death; his account connects the dead physician with the philosopher van Halm.

articles.title: Farmiga
articles.ru: Don Farmiga
articles.summary: Dean of the Faculty of Letters at the Academy of Arts and Alvaro’s superior; a strict administrator who refuses salary advances.

articles.title: Fatima Ir-Reya
articles.ru: Fatima Ir-Reya, prim-allen of the esfera of Law
articles.summary: Prim-allen of the esfera of Law, Catalia’s most influential lawyer, and one of the heroes of the Solantan Expedition about whom Alvaro writes a book commissioned by Filippe.

articles.title: Fernan Gereira
articles.ru: Fernan Gereira
articles.summary: A street scribe from the esfera of Service, Alvaro's friend and later secretary; a committed reformist who dreams of reshaping the High Table.

articles.title: Filippe di Berro
articles.ru: Don Filippe di Berro, prim-allen of the esfera of Art
articles.summary: An operatic tenor and prim-allen of the esfera of Art who commissions the book about the heroes of the Solantan Expedition; a vindictive, calculating patron on whom Alvaro da Silva’s career depends.
searchAliases: Дон Филиппе ди Берро, прим-аллен эсферы Искусства

articles.title: Flammel
articles.ru: Oberfischmeister Flammel
articles.summary: The Fishermen’s Guild oberfischmeister whom Magnus Amir the Grey placed in charge of investigating the destruction of Dunkwald. He interrogated Joriksen.

articles.title: Franz Freiber
articles.ru: Franz Freiber (“Fra-Fra”)
articles.summary: A fair-haired Hofstadt rogue whom Dietrich knows from queues at government offices. He advises Dietrich to seek recommendations and offers the lieutenant a “temporary” occupation, which he angrily rejects.

articles.title: Frey
articles.ru: Frey
articles.summary: Fatima Ir-Reya’s gloomy chauffeur and bodyguard; a good shot who appears beside her employer at the most dangerous moments.

articles.title: Gelb
articles.ru: Gelb, noncommissioned officer
articles.summary: A cruel noncommissioned officer commanding the platoon of stone fusiliers attached to Dietrich von Dort’s battery. The stones escape during the night after nailing him to a wall, and he dies.

articles.title: Frau Gieseke
articles.ru: Frau Gieseke, owner of the house on Witwenplatz
articles.summary: Dietrich and Mari’s landlady in Hofstadt’s Widows’ District. A widow descended from Empress Augusta’s first widows, she adores Dietrich like a son and is certain that Mari will soon be widowed.
searchAliases: Фрау Гизеке, хозяйка дома на Витвенплац

articles.title: Greta
articles.ru: Greta, a slave from the women's hamlet in Dunkwald
articles.summary: A slave from the women's hamlet at the Dangarian camp, Red's “prize” for the well; she becomes his lover, teaches him Dangarian and faith in the Sower, and eventually ends up in the beast's pit.
searchAliases: Грета, рабыня с женского хутора в Дунквальде

articles.title: Isabel el Niña
articles.ru: Doña Isabel el Niña
articles.summary: The wife of the smuggler Carlos el Niña, a sickly, quiet woman whose disappearance becomes one of the mysteries in the first half of the novel.

articles.title: Fritjof Joriksen
articles.ru: Fritjof Joriksen, master fisherman (fischmeister)
articles.summary: A Dangarian master fisherman of the Guild who links Red's and Dietrich's storylines: as a young fischmeister, he made the Catalian dig a well in Dunkwald; later, in Ollandia, he gets Lieutenant von Dort on his hook.

articles.title: The Kaiser
articles.ru: The Kaiser (emperor) of Dangar
articles.summary: Dangar’s ruler, who is neither named nor shown in person in the novel. His will is invoked to explain the war in Ollandia, appointments, and noble marriages; according to the author, court affairs will appear only in the second book.

articles.title: Carlos el Niña
articles.ru: Carlos el Niña, don of the esfera of Shadow
articles.summary: A former corsair, now a smuggler and don of the esfera of Shadow, who owns the fort in Laerta's Old Port; the first of the heroes of the Solantan Expedition about whom Alvaro da Silva is writing a book.
searchAliases: Карлос эль Нинья, дон эсферы Тени

articles.title: Carmensita Estevos
articles.ru: Carmensita Estevos (Kara), obrero of the esfera of Shadow and mother of Red’s son
articles.summary: A woman from a harbor brothel in Laerta and mother of the son of Rodrigo da Vira — Red. In his storyline she is Kara; in the Great Scroll’s records she is Carmensita Estevos, who sought recognition as da Vira’s widow.
searchAliases: Карменсита Эстевос (Кара), обреро эсферы Тени, мать сына Рэда

articles.title: Katrina von Lurd
articles.ru: Katrina von Lurd, née von Eyring, countess
articles.summary: A countess, wife of Deputy Foreign Minister Ludwig von Lurd, born von Eyring. Olkha’s best friend and Dietrich’s “sister” in their invented cover story. She has a secret that forces her to protect her “brother.”
searchAliases: Катрина фон Лурд, урождённая фон Эйринг, графиня

articles.title: Heinz von Dort
articles.ru: Heinz von Dort, son of Dietrich and Mari
aliases: little orphan (Frau Gieseke’s name for him)
articles.summary: Dietrich and Mari von Dort’s infant son. He does almost nothing himself in the plot, but his name is entered as collateral in Joriksen’s pledge: if the debt is not paid, the child can be made a stone.
searchAliases: Хайнц фон Дорт, сын Дитриха и Мари

articles.title: Javier Salam
articles.ru: Javier Salam, nicknamed Need Anything
articles.summary: A driver and tour guide from Tres Molinos who shows visitors the House Above and sells information one installment at a time.
searchAliases: Хавьер Салам по прозвищу Чего-Нибудь Нужно

articles.title: Hofmeyer
articles.ru: Hofmeyer, lieutenant general of the Dangarian army
articles.summary: A Dangarian lieutenant general commanding the army that advances into eastern Ollandia and besieges the fortress of Mershants near Catalia's borders. One of three army commanders and, in the judgment of the narrator and Deserey, the most capable.

articles.title: Jose Flarbo
articles.ru: Señor Jose Flarbo, bookseller
articles.summary: The cheerful elderly owner of a basement bookshop near the Academy of Arts, who tells Alvaro the story of the philosopher van Halm.

articles.title: Garcia Juanes
articles.ru: Garcia Juanes, doctor
articles.summary: A physician in the capital and ship’s doctor aboard the Santa Eliza during the Solantan Expedition; his strange death in Laerta's white district begins Alvaro da Silva's investigation.

articles.title: Wolfgang von Klein
articles.ru: Wolfgang (Wolf) von Klein, a Kaiser’s Claw
articles.summary: An officer of Dangar's special service (a “Kaiser’s Claw”), known to Red as the Black Falcon. He serves as a lieutenant in Dunkwald and later, as a major, interrogates Dietrich in Latsen.

articles.title: Cristobal Maduro
articles.ru: Don Cristobal Maduro, manufacturer
articles.summary: An arms manufacturer of the esfera of Production, one of the heroes of the Solantan Expedition, and an opponent of the reformists; he does not appear in person in the novel, but his men threaten Alvaro.

articles.title: Kurtzleben
articles.ru: Kurtzleben, General of Infantry
articles.summary: A Dangarian general of infantry commanding the southern army in Ollandia, the strongest of the three. The narrator calls him a ruthless butcher with an iron will; he is the man who captured Ollandia's capital, Bargot.

articles.title: Landau
articles.ru: Friedrich von Landau, baron, oberfischmeister of Dunkwald
articles.summary: A Dangarian baron and senior master fisherman sent to command Dunkwald; a physician and oberfischmeister with a special power, who devises the beast’s Zustand for Red.
searchAliases: Фридрих фон Ландау, барон, обер-фишмайстер Дунквальда

articles.title: Wladyslaw Lenz
articles.ru: Prince Wladyslaw Lenz, marshal of the nobility of the Latsen Voivodeship
articles.summary: An Ollandian prince, descendant of an ancient family, and marshal of the nobility of the Latsen Voivodeship. He surrendered the voivodeship to the Dangarians without a fight and is now seeking appointment in Hofstadt as the Kaiser's governor in Ollandia. Olkha's uncle and guardian.
searchAliases: Князь Владислав Ленц, предводитель дворянства Лаценского воеводства

articles.title: Lid Anteodor
articles.ru: Lid Anteodor, “Hidalgo Lid”
articles.summary: A legendary Catalian knight and hero of numerous tales. He does not appear in person in the novel: he is recalled as a symbol of victory against hopeless odds, while Red values his flexibility.

articles.title: Liess van Halm
articles.ru: Liess van Halm, philosopher
articles.summary: A philosopher from Mergana and author of the unfinished Philosophy of Horror; he lost his sanity at his estate in Selezia, and his fate proves connected with the five heroes of Solanta.

articles.title: Ludwig von Lurd
articles.ru: Count Ludwig von Lurd, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs
articles.summary: A Dangarian count of about fifty, deputy minister of foreign affairs and effectively the head of the ministry. Katrina's husband and the Kaiser's adviser on dynastic marriages. He devises a way out of the scandal and sends Dietrich and Olkha to the altar.
searchAliases: Граф Людвиг фон Лурд, товарищ министра иностранных дел

articles.title: Lucille Gereira
articles.ru: Lucille Gereira
articles.summary: Fernan's wife, a nanny from the esfera of Service; Alvaro's practical, kindhearted friend, who feeds both men and reins in his vanity.

articles.title: Malena
articles.ru: Malena
articles.summary: The owner of a book café in Laerta, Alvaro's longtime lover and kind friend.

articles.title: Little One
articles.ru: Little One
articles.summary: A giant obrero with a mechanical steam-powered arm, an associate of Mor; in ch. 11, Alvaro mistakes him for Mor himself.

articles.title: Mari von Dort
articles.ru: Mari von Dort, wife of Lieutenant Dietrich von Dort
articles.summary: Dietrich von Dort’s wife and mother of his son Heinz, a frugal, strong-willed Dangarian woman from an impoverished noble family. Her fear of hardship drives Dietrich to spend their last savings on fishing in a Well, beginning his path toward a schönbrun of his own.
searchAliases: Мари фон Дорт, жена поручика Дитриха фон Дорта

articles.title: Senora Marques
articles.ru: Senora Marques, owner of a coffee shop in Tres Molinos
articles.summary: The owner of a tiny coffee shop and “museum of misfortunes” in Tres Molinos, an expert on the history of the cursed House Above.
searchAliases: Сеньора Маркес, хозяйка кофейни в Трес Молиносе

articles.title: Milosh
articles.ru: Milosh, Dietrich von Dort’s orderly
articles.summary: A stone slave and Dietrich von Dort’s orderly, whom Dietrich received from his father. A talkative, mocking, cunning servant who accompanies his master in war and in the capital and rescues him from awkward situations.

articles.title: Mor
articles.ru: Mor, chief engineer of the Esperanza factory
articles.summary: One of the leaders of the reformists in Laerta, an engineer from Brega who founded the Esperanza factory and asks Alvaro for help in a dispute with the manufacturers.

articles.title: Nivendey
articles.ru: Nivendey, Red's cellmate
articles.summary: Red's talkative cellmate before the execution, whom Red mentions to Greta; the name also appears in Senora Marques's story about the House Above.

articles.title: Olkha Lenz
articles.ru: Olkha Lenz, princess (“Helga in your language”)
articles.summary: An Ollandian princess from Latsen, niece and ward of Prince Wladyslaw Lenz. An awkward, teasing, brave young woman whose fate is connected with Lieutenant Dietrich von Dort.

articles.title: Wasp
articles.ru: Wasp (pseudonym)
aliases: the boy with the yellow ribbon
articles.summary: An Academy of Arts student and young Reformist who idolizes Alvaro and delivers Mor’s messages to him.

articles.title: Otto
articles.ru: Otto, Fritjof Joriksen’s secretary and pupil
articles.summary: A pale, talkative young man, secretary and pupil to Fischmeister Joriksen. He knows the map of the Wells east of the capital by heart and chatters incessantly.
searchAliases: Отто, секретарь и ученик Фритьофа Йориксена

articles.title: Young Scribe
articles.ru: The young scribe, a scribe's assistant at Joriksen's camp
articles.summary: A pimply young scribe who records Zustands and the depths of pits, later prays to Red, and returns years afterward as a future fischmeister intending to buy Greta.
searchAliases: Писарёнок, помощник писаря в лагере Йориксена

articles.title: Reiniger
articles.ru: Field Marshal Reiniger, commander of the Dangarian forces in Ollandia
articles.summary: A Dangarian field marshal commanding all forces in the Ollandian theater of war. Headquartered in Latsen, he revises the campaign plan and divides Hofmeyer’s army.
searchAliases: Фельдмаршал Райнигер, командующий дангарскими войсками в Олландии

articles.title: Red
articles.ru: Red, a Catalian from Laerta
articles.summary: A Catalian enslaved in Dangar, one of the novel's three main protagonists; his storyline takes place before the others and centers on the camp of enslaved well-diggers in Dunkwald.

articles.title: Ricardo Flores
articles.ru: Don Ricardo Flores
articles.summary: Alvaro's grandfather, author of the novel The Snake in the Reeds, and the only member of the Flores family whose name is inscribed on the Great Scroll.

articles.title: Salvador
articles.ru: Salvador, Don Maduro’s mercenary
aliases: the attacker in the Old Port
articles.summary: A guard and mercenary employed by the manufacturer Maduro, who interrogates Alvaro at the mansion and pursues the writer, demanding that he abandon the book.

articles.title: Speer
articles.ru: Speer, lieutenant, commander of the battery’s first platoon
articles.summary: A lieutenant from the estate of hares, commanding the first platoon in Staff Captain Zeidvist’s battery. Under regulations, he should have assumed command after the captain’s death, but submits to Dietrich.
searchAliases: Шпеер, поручик, командир первого взвода батареи

articles.title: Schultz
articles.ru: Schultz, the red-haired slave from Red’s dugout
articles.summary: A red-haired slave with a split eyebrow from Red’s first dugout; the only one of his bunkmates named in the text, and a living illustration of the price stones pay.
searchAliases: Шульц, рыжий раб из землянки Рэда

articles.title: Hoarse
articles.ru: Hoarse, a slave from Red's dugout
articles.summary: One of the foreman's four subordinates in Red's first dugout, a slave whose voice fails him and who prays in the evenings.

articles.title: Salvation
articles.ru: Salvation, a holy-fool stone slave
articles.summary: A holy-fool stone slave in the fusilier platoon, with absolute faith in the Sower and the “dear water.” The only one who does not escape with the platoon, and the only man Dietrich kills with his own hand after the battle.

articles.title: Enhal
articles.ru: Don Enhal, first-level judge
articles.summary: A first-level judge and Beatriz’s father; a patient, tactful man who writes letters on his daughter’s behalf and protects her.

articles.title: The One Without Nails
articles.ru: The One Without Nails, a slave from Red's dugout
articles.summary: A slave from Red's first dugout with fingers scraped raw; he digs a well at the camp with his bare hands.
searchAliases: Тот Без Ногтей, раб из землянки Рэда

articles.title: Ugo Martinez
articles.ru: Ugo Martinez
articles.summary: A hired chauffeur whom Alvaro and Fernan mistakenly take for a spy; he divorced his wife that day.

articles.title: Friedrich von Wahrheit
articles.ru: Count Friedrich von Wahrheit, newspaper owner
articles.summary: A Dangarian count who owns four newspapers, including Glory of the Empire, and is close to the Kaiser. He enjoys flattery and the card game Stoss.
searchAliases: Граф Фридрих фон Вархайт, владелец газет

articles.title: Wiglaf
articles.ru: Wiglaf, Master Joriksen's assistant
articles.summary: Fischmeister Joriksen's assistant during the fishing party at Baroness Walbrecht's: a burly man with thick sideburns and an anchor on his shoulder.

articles.title: Vincente Ramires da Rimini
articles.ru: Vincente Ramires da Rimini
articles.summary: A master of law from Fatima the allen’s circle who insults Alvaro in the first chapter and wins seven thousand escudos from him in a dueling debate.

articles.title: Second Killer
articles.ru: Unnamed rifleman, Salvador’s accomplice
articles.summary: An unnamed gunman with a bolt-action rifle who acts alongside Salvador during the assault on Last Winter and is captured alive.
searchAliases: Безымянный стрелок с винтовкой, сообщник Сальвадора

articles.title: Yakka
articles.ru: Yakka, a free hunter serving Fischmeister Joriksen
articles.summary: A free northern hunter in Fischmeister Joriksen's service, an escort and the master's “left hand”; Red's guard, rescuer, and ultimately former friend.
searchAliases: Якка, вольный охотник при фишмайстере Йориксене

articles.title: Claus von Zeidvist
articles.ru: Claus von Zeidvist, staff captain
articles.summary: A staff captain commanding a Dangarian battery in the Ollandian rear, and Dietrich von Dort's superior. A harsh commander whom his subordinates consider fond of schnapps; he is killed by a stray bullet, a death the text suggests Dietrich himself predicted.

articles.title: Golden Ducat
articles.ru: Golden Ducat, Carlos el Niña’s quartermaster
articles.summary: Carlos el Niña’s quartermaster, a pirate with a gold tooth and one of Alvaro’s tavern friends.
searchAliases: Золотой Дукат, квартирмейстер Карлоса эль Ниньи

articles.title: Ai-Khinar
articles.ru: Ai-Khinar — the most fearsome of the Ancients, a winged serpent
articles.summary: Ai-Khinar is one of the Lords of the Abyss, “the most fearsome of the Ancients,” a winged venomous serpent. His statue stands at the entrance to Laerta’s Old Port and serves as the district’s symbol.
searchAliases: Ай-Хинар — самый грозный из Древних, крылатый змей

articles.title: Alessina
articles.ru: Alessina — mirna of art and creativity
articles.summary: Alessina is the mirna of art, patroness of writers, painters, and actors. Her name appears in oaths and greetings, and Laerta’s grand waterfront bay is named after her.

articles.title: Alguacils
articles.ru: Alguacils — Catalian detectives and legal officers of the esfera of Law
articles.summary: Alguacils are one of Catalia’s two law enforcement services. Guards from the esfera of Shadow intervene when an offense is obvious; alguacils from the esfera of Law determine whether the letter of the Scroll has been violated and who is responsible.

articles.title: Allens
articles.ru: Allens — representatives of the esferas at the High Table
articles.summary: The highest representatives of the Catalian esferas: each esfera sends three allens to the High Table. Allens handle the country’s foreign affairs and settle disputes between esferas; they include Fatima Ir-Reya (Law) and Don Filippe di Berro (Art).
searchAliases: Аллены — представители эсфер за Высоким Столом

articles.title: White, Grey, and Black Land
articles.ru: White, grey, and black land — zones of permissible violence in Catalia
articles.summary: Catalian districts are divided into white (no crime at all), grey (theft, fraud, and fighting are allowed, but killing is not), and black (almost anything is permitted). Murder on white land is the country’s greatest taboo.
searchAliases: Белая, серая и чёрная земля — зоны допустимого насилия в Каталии

articles.title: Bracelets
articles.ru: Bracelets — signs of esfera and rank in Catalia
articles.summary: Catalians wear bracelets that immediately reveal their esfera and rank: a silver bracelet for a maestro, gold for a don, black with gears for an engineer. A bracelet can be earned, challenged, and lost in a debate.
searchAliases: Браслеты — знаки эсферы и ранга в Каталии

articles.title: Darreggio
articles.ru: Darreggio — mirn of mechanics and engineering
articles.summary: Darreggio is one of the few males among the mirnas, the patron of mechanics and engineering. His figurine strikes three in the afternoon on the tower of the Academy of Arts; his temple stands in Laerta’s Craftsmen’s Square.

articles.title: Money
articles.ru: Money and prices in Catalia and Dangar
articles.summary: In Catalia, accounts are reckoned in escudos and small change is called pesetas and pesos; in Dangar, people pay in marks. Amounts in the novel often drive the plot: the stake in a dueling debate, Alvaro’s fees, and the price of fishing with Joriksen.
searchAliases: Деньги и цены в Каталии и Дангаре

articles.title: Ancients
articles.ru: The Ancients, also known as the Lords of the Abyss (the Winged Ones) — Catalia’s ancient gods
articles.summary: The Ancients are the sea gods and monsters of the old Catalian faith, the creators of humanity. Their names survive in oaths, curses, and ornamentation, while their temples have remained closed since the time of the First Judge.
searchAliases: Древние, они же Владыки бездны (Крылатые) — древние боги Каталии

articles.title: Dueling Debate
articles.ru: Dueling debate — a public contest of arguments under the First Judge’s code
aliases: contest in the Chamber of the Word
articles.summary: Catalia’s principal way of resolving conflicts and establishing truths: the parties speak before an arbiter and jurors in the Chamber of the Word, and the result is recorded on the Great Scroll. Catalians, “people of the word,” prefer debate to a duel with weapons.
searchAliases: Дуэльный спор — публичный поединок доводов по кодексу Первого Судьи

articles.title: Eikha
articles.ru: Eikha — the hunter Yakka’s double-barreled flintlock, “with a soul and a charm”
articles.summary: Eikha is the hunter Yakka’s old double-barreled flintlock, decorated with silver. Yakka believes that a soul lives within it and that the gun is protected by a charm; when parting from Red, he says that he will consult Eikha.
searchAliases: Эйкха — двуствольное кремнёвое ружьё охотника Якки, «с душой и заговором»

articles.title: Eliga
articles.ru: Eliga — the two-faced mirna of luck
articles.summary: Eliga is the mirna of luck and chance, whose name Catalians invoke in every game and misfortune. Red wears her as a tattoo on his arm, and Alvaro uses her to explain several of the novel’s mysteries.

articles.title: Esferas
articles.ru: Esferas — Catalia’s professional estates
articles.summary: The eleven professional communities into which Catalia is divided. Each esfera is almost self-governing, has three allens at the High Table, and maintains its own ranks and bracelets; a person belongs to an esfera through their trade, not by birth.

articles.title: Esperanza
articles.ru: Esperanza — a compact steam engine factory and Beatriz’s steam carriage
articles.summary: Esperanza is a factory in Brega built jointly by laid-off workers, and the brand of its compact steam engines. Beatriz’s red Esperanza becomes the protagonists’ main means of transport.
searchAliases: «Эсперанца» — завод компактных паровых моторов и паровой экипаж Беатрис

articles.title: Philosophy of Horror
articles.ru: “Philosophy of Horror” — Liess van Halm’s unfinished book and an exhibition of paintings based on it
aliases: Philosophy of Horror. An Artist’s View of the Myths of the Ancients
articles.summary: “Philosophy of Horror” is the last, unfinished book by the Merganan philosopher Liess van Halm, and an exhibition of paintings with the same name at the Eliste Gallery. The title continually resurfaces in Alvaro’s investigation.
searchAliases: «Философия ужаса» — неоконченная книга Лиесса ван Хальма и выставка картин по ней
выставка «Философия ужаса. Авторский взгляд на мифы о Древних»

articles.title: Fischmeisters
articles.ru: Fischmeisters — the guild’s master fishermen, who work with wells
articles.summary: Dangarian masters of “fishing” in Beautiful Wells, members of the Fishermen’s Guild. They determine whether a well has been dug successfully, conduct fishing sessions for the nobility, and seek a way to create a schönbrun.
searchAliases: Фишмайстеры — мастера-рыбаки гильдии, работающие с колодцами

articles.title: Glossary
articles.ru: World of Wells glossary — titles, ranks, money, faith, technology, and local words
articles.summary: An alphabetical dictionary of the words and concepts in Traces on the Water: Catalian ranks and bracelets, Dangarian estates and military ranks, coins and measures, beliefs, wells and fishing, technology, Spanish and German words, nicknames, and customs.
searchAliases: Глоссарий мира колодцев — титулы, чины, деньги, вера, техника и местные слова

articles.title: Iolanta
articles.ru: Iolanta — mirna of Law
articles.summary: Iolanta is the mirna of Law, a celebrated debater. Her symbol is a white feather, and members of the esfera of Law—judges, lawyers, and alguacils—are called “servants of Iolanta.”

articles.title: Stones
articles.ru: Stones (Steins) — Dangar’s slave estate
articles.summary: Dangar’s slaves, the lowest of the empire’s three estates. Stones perform almost all menial labor, make up the army’s rank and file, dig wells, and are considered the Sower’s favored estate: according to scripture, they have been freed from responsibility and choice.

articles.title: Wells
articles.ru: Wells, or schönbruns (“Beautiful Wells”) — windows into another world
articles.summary: Mysterious wells in which mist and another world inhabited by monsters can be seen instead of water. Dangarians regard them as a source of miracles and dig in search of them, while Catalians see them as curiosities; all three of the novel’s storylines revolve around wells.
searchAliases: Колодцы, или шёнбруны («Прекрасные Колодцы») — окна в иной мир

articles.title: Dangarian Culture
articles.ru: Dangarian culture — faith, life within the estates, the court, and imperial high society
articles.summary: How Dangarians live: the etiquette of eagles, hares, and stones; a church with slave priests and the feeding ritual; fishing as a social amusement; newspapers, the court, and attitudes toward foreigners. A supplement to the article about the state.
searchAliases: Культура Дангара — вера, сословный быт, двор и светская жизнь империи

articles.title: Catalian Culture
articles.ru: Catalian culture — the daily life, art, rituals, and manners of the people of the word
articles.summary: How Catalians live: professional esferas in place of traditional estates, debate in place of dueling, freedom of speech, art, rituals, and wine. A supplement to the articles about the state and its institutions.
searchAliases: Культура Каталии — быт, искусство, обряды и нравы людей слова

articles.title: Ollandia and the Ollandians
articles.ru: Ollandia and the Ollandians — the people’s customs, names, and character
articles.summary: What is known about Ollandian customs and character: proud princes and voivodeships, hussars, Slavic names, and similarities to the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth noted by the author; the novel offers relatively little material.
searchAliases: Олландия и олландцы — обычаи, имена и облик народа

articles.title: World of Wells
articles.ru: World of Wells—the setting of the novel Traces on the Water
aliases: the world of Traces on the Water
articles.summary: An overview of the fictional world of Traces on the Water: Catalia and Dangar, Ollandia and neighboring lands, esferas, bracelets and slavery, wells and fishing, beliefs, technology and history, and the world's connection to the author's other worlds.
searchAliases: Мир колодцев — мир романа «Следы на воде»

articles.title: Mirnas
articles.ru: Mirnas (mirna, mirn) — female and male patrons of fields of human activity in Catalian tradition
articles.summary: Mirnas are the semi-mythical patrons of Catalian pursuits and forces: luck, art, law, engineering, and fertility. They are not prayed to as gods, but are invoked in oaths, honored with temples and statues, and used as symbols of the esferas.
searchAliases: Мирны (мирна, мирн) — покровительницы и покровители сфер человеческой деятельности в каталийской традиции

articles.title: Obreros
articles.ru: Obreros — Catalia’s ordinary workers, the lowest rank of the esferas
articles.summary: The ordinary workers of the esferas, chiefly the Three Bulls: factory workers, peasants, and servants. This is the lowest rank in the bracelet system; in the novel, obreros lose their jobs to steam-powered machinery and try to defeat the factory owners in debate.
searchAliases: Обреро — рядовые работники Каталии, нижний ранг эсфер

articles.title: Eagles and Hares
articles.ru: Eagles and hares — Dangar’s nobles and free commoners, who together with the stones form the empire’s three estates
articles.summary: Dangar’s two upper estates out of three. Eagles are the nobility and officer class, with the name particle “von”; hares are free townspeople, merchants, managers, and clerks. Below both stand the slave stones.
searchAliases: Орлы и зайцы — дворянство и свободные простолюдины Дангара (вместе с камнями — три сословия империи)

articles.title: References to Polari
articles.ru: References to the Polari series in the novel “Traces on the Water”
articles.summary: Echoes of Roman Surzhikov’s earlier Polari series in the novel: Alvaro, writing a book about living people, recalls the “author within the world” of the collector’s edition of “Arrow, Coin, Spark,” while the author directly connected General Deserey’s demolition of Alvaro’s novel with real criticism of Polari. Other similarities are less certain, and each is marked with its degree of confidence.
searchAliases: Отсылки к циклу «Полари» в романе «Следы на воде»

articles.title: First Judge
articles.ru: The First Judge — creator of modern Catalia, the code of dueling debates, and the Great Scroll
articles.summary: The semi-legendary founder of the Catalian order. Under his code, Catalians settle conflicts through debate; he created the Great Scroll, abolished the paganism of the Ancients, and gave the country principles engraved on slabs in the Hall of the Scroll.
searchAliases: Первый Судья — создатель современной Каталии, кодекса дуэльных споров и Великого Свитка

articles.title: Models and Influences
articles.ru: Models and influences — what the countries and institutions of the World of Wells resemble
articles.summary: What the author himself named as models for the World of Wells—Catalia’s Spanish style, Dangar’s German and Prussian style, the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth for Ollandia, and Lovecraft for the Ancients—and which analogies a reader can see in the text.
searchAliases: Прообразы и влияния — на что похожи страны и порядки мира колодцев

articles.title: Roman Surzhikov
articles.ru: Roman Surzhikov — author of “Traces on the Water” and the Polari series
articles.summary: A contemporary fantasy author, creator of Polari and the World of Wells. This article collects information about him relevant to “Traces on the Water,” based on his own words in two streams with readers.
searchAliases: Роман Суржиков — автор романа «Следы на воде» и цикла «Полари»

articles.title: Airship
articles.ru: Airship — a flying ship in the World of Wells
articles.summary: An airship in the World of Wells is not an airplane, but a flying ship with masts, cannons, and bells. It is kept aloft by brante wood, which produces lift as long as it has not dried out. In the novel, Dangar has airships, while Catalia is only beginning to build them.

articles.title: Santa Eliza
articles.ru: Santa Eliza — Captain Carlos el Niña’s ship on the Solantan expedition
articles.summary: Santa Eliza is the ship on which Captain Carlos el Niña sailed on the Solantan expedition. Its crew is connected with the five heroes of Solanta about whom Alvaro writes a book, and with the navigator Rodrigo da Vira.
searchAliases: «Санта Элиза» — корабль Солантийской экспедиции капитана Карлоса эль Ниньи

articles.title: Sower
articles.ru: The Sower — Dangar’s one god, the All-Good
articles.summary: The one god of Dangarian religion, who created humanity and the estates through the parable of the field, and miracles through a well of faith. Every estate of Dangar professes belief in him, and that faith explains the empire’s structure, the slavery of the stones, and the holiness of Beautiful Wells.

articles.title: Sinkho
articles.ru: Sinkho — a small mourning tree with ribbons
articles.summary: A sinkho is a dry tree in a pot on the porch, a sign of a recent death in the house. Anyone wishing to express their feelings about the deceased may tie a blue, red, or black ribbon to it.

articles.title: The Author's Words
articles.ru: The Author's Words—what Roman Surzhikov said about Traces on the Water and the World of Wells in livestreams
aliases: Surzhikov on Traces on the Water
articles.summary: A summary of what Roman Surzhikov said about Traces on the Water and the World of Wells in two reader Q&A livestreams: the conception, models for the countries, characters, unrevealed mysteries, the continuation, and publication.
searchAliases: Слово автора — что Роман Суржиков рассказывал о «Следах на воде» и мире колодцев на стримах

articles.title: Great Scroll
articles.ru: The Great Scroll — Catalia’s register of judicial truths
articles.summary: The repository of the results of every judicial debate in Catalia since the First Judge’s time. Everything that wins a debate becomes “Truth” on the Scroll and has the force of law; a record cannot be forged or destroyed, only challenged through a new debate.
searchAliases: Великий Свиток — каталийский реестр судебных истин

articles.title: Technology
articles.ru: Technology and weapons in the world of “Traces on the Water”
articles.summary: The novel’s world is an age of steam and gunpowder: steam carriages and machinery, railways, revolvers, and breech-loading rifles in Catalia; flintlock muskets, cannons, and flying ships in Dangar.
searchAliases: Техника и оружие мира «Следов на воде»

articles.title: Dark Schönbrun
articles.ru: Dark schönbrun — a well of misfortune
articles.summary: A type of well in which fishing is dangerous: a dark schönbrun harms the body, reason, feelings, and prosperity. In the Catalian storyline, such a well stands in Last Winter castle, and its workings are expressed in the “three laws of the well of misfortune.”

articles.title: Esfera of Shadow
articles.ru: The esfera of Shadow — Catalia’s estate of criminal trades
articles.summary: One of Catalia’s eleven esferas, uniting thieves, swindlers, pirates, assassins, prostitutes, and other trades outside the law. Catalia does not exterminate criminals, but recognizes them as an estate with its own districts, rules, and seats at the High Table.
searchAliases: Эсфера Тени — каталийское сословие преступных ремёсел

articles.title: Quotations
articles.ru: Quotations from the novel “Traces on the Water”
articles.summary: Short, memorable lines spoken by characters in “Traces on the Water,” grouped by speaker, with chapter numbers and explanations of the situations in which they occur.

articles.title: Zustand
articles.ru: Zustand — a condition assigned to a slave; a method of digging a well
articles.summary: The Dangarian word for a working condition announced to slave “stones” by scribes. For well diggers, a Zustand is a particular set of mandatory digging conditions tailored to an individual’s “essence.”
searchAliases: Цуштанд — условие, назначенное рабу; способ копки колодца

articles.title: The Herald
articles.ru: The Herald (Laerta Herald) — a newspaper of the capital
articles.summary: The Herald is a Laertan newspaper sold by boys on the boulevards. In the novel, it reports on strikes, judicial debates, and famous people, while workers regard it as bought and paid for.

articles.title: Vinsenya
articles.ru: Vinsenya — mirna of fertility
articles.summary: Vinsenya is the mirna of fertility, one of the mirna clock figures on the balcony of Laerta’s Academy of Arts. A church bears her name, and she is painted asleep on the walls of working-class districts.

articles.title: High Table
articles.ru: The High Table — Catalia’s supreme body, an assembly of allens from every esfera
articles.summary: The body that has governed Catalia since the First Judge’s time. Every esfera is represented by three allens; the Table decides foreign policy and disputes between esferas, but does not interfere in their internal affairs.
searchAliases: Высокий Стол — верховный орган Каталии, собрание алленов всех эсфер

articles.title: Languages
articles.ru: Languages of the World of Wells—Catalian, Dangarian, Ollandian, Merganan, Muari, and Solantan
articles.summary: The languages of the World of Wells, who speaks them, the real-world languages they resemble—Catalian is Spanish, Dangarian is German—and the words from them that appear in the novel's Russian text.
searchAliases: Языки мира колодцев — каталийский, дангарский, олландский, мерганский, муарийский и солантийский

articles.title: The Dueling Debate with Ramires
articles.ru: The Dueling Debate Between Alvaro da Silva and Vincente Ramires da Rimini in the Chamber of the Word
aliases: debate in the Chamber of the Word
articles.summary: The novel’s opening action: offended on his friends’ behalf, the writer Alvaro challenges the legal master Ramires to a dueling debate, loses a month’s income, and consequently accepts Don Filippe’s commission for a book about the heroes of Solanta.
searchAliases: Дуэльный спор Альваро да Силвы и Винсенте Рамиреса да Римини в Палате Слова

articles.title: The Destruction of Dunkwald
articles.ru: The Destruction of the Fishermen’s Settlement of Dunkwald
articles.summary: The sudden death of everyone in the Fishermen’s Guild’s forest settlement, which Dietrich learns about first from a newspaper and then from Magnus the Grey. The novel does not name the cause, and the guild’s investigation reaches a dead end.

articles.title: The Ollandian War
articles.ru: The Dangarian Invasion of Ollandia
articles.summary: The war in which the Dangarian Empire defeated the Principality of Ollandia with three armies and reached Catalia’s borders. It provides the background to Dietrich’s storyline and determines the stakes in several Catalian chapters.

articles.title: The Night at Last Winter
articles.ru: Solving the Mystery of van Halm’s Castle and the Fight at Last Winter
articles.summary: The novel’s final scene: Alvaro and Fernan discover the explanation for the castle’s “curse,” two killers attack them, and events in the cellar beside the dark schönbrun end with Fatima’s arrival and her account of the rest.
searchAliases: Разгадка тайны замка ван Хальма и схватка в «Последней Зиме»

articles.title: Fishing at Baroness Walbrecht’s
articles.ru: Fishing in Baroness Elsa von Walbrecht’s Beautiful Well and the Ball That Follows
articles.summary: The only schönbrun “fishing” session shown in detail in the novel: Master Joriksen fishes for a miracle for thirty-six spectators, including Dietrich. The baroness’s reception brings him together with Joriksen, Prince Lenz, and Olkha.
searchAliases: Рыбалка в Прекрасном Колодце баронессы Эльзы фон Вальбрехт и бал после неё

articles.title: The Death of Dr. Juanes
articles.ru: The Death of Dr. Garcia Juanes, Ship’s Physician of the Santa Eliza
articles.summary: The sudden death of a hero of the Solantan expedition in a white district of Laerta, where murder is impossible under the laws of the land. Alvaro sees the beginning of a detective story, and the solution proves to be a chain of accidents with a deeper cause.
searchAliases: Смерть доктора Гарсии Хуанеса, судового врача «Санта Элизы»

articles.title: The Solantan Expedition
articles.ru: The Solantan Expedition of the Catalian Schooner Santa Eliza
aliases: the exploit of the heroes of Solanta
articles.summary: The past event that made five Catalians famous: the schooner Santa Eliza broke through to Solanta, captured a coastal fort, and forced the doge to sign a treaty. The official account differs from what actually happened.

articles.title: Obrero Unrest in Laerta
articles.ru: The Obrero Protest Against Steam-Powered Machinery and the Strike at Laerta’s Factories
articles.summary: A series of protests by Laerta’s workers against dismissals caused by steam-powered machines: a lost debate in the Chamber of the Word, a railway barricade, violence by guards and Shadows, and then a factory strike. Alvaro is drawn into events against his will.
searchAliases: Протест обреро против паровых станков и стачка на заводах Лаэрты

articles.title: The Battle at the Well on the Hill
articles.ru: The Battle Between a Dangarian Battery and an Ollandian Hussar Squadron (“Three Volleys of Canister”)
articles.summary: The battle in which Lieutenant Dietrich von Dort, after looking into a well, commands his battery as though he knows the course of events in advance and destroys a hussar squadron with three volleys of canister. The victory makes Dietrich a hero, then a suspect.
searchAliases: Бой дангарской батареи с олландским гусарским эскадроном («Три залпа картечью»)

articles.title: Dangar
articles.ru: The Dangarian Empire
articles.summary: A slaveholding empire in the west of the known world, governed by rank, faith in the Sower, and the labor of enslaved stones; Dietrich von Dort’s homeland and the place of Red’s penal servitude.

articles.title: Fishermen’s Guild
articles.ru: The Guild (Order) of Fishermen, the Fischmeisters of the Dangarian Empire
articles.summary: A Dangarian community of masters who know how to “fish” in magical wells called schönbruns. One of the empire’s three powers, alongside the Kaiser and the patriarch; it owns Dunkwald’s enslaved diggers, who have spent half a century unsuccessfully trying to create a schönbrun.

articles.title: Catalia
articles.ru: Catalia (Colloquially “Beautiful and Mighty Catalia”)
aliases: land of the people of the word
land of steam engines and rifled barrels
articles.summary: A coastal country in the southeast of the known world, Alvaro da Silva’s homeland: a society without hereditary nobility, divided into esferas, where every dispute is settled by a verbal contest in the Chamber of the Word.
searchAliases: страна паровых машин и нарезных стволов

articles.title: Kaiser’s Claws
articles.ru: The “Kaiser’s Claws” Special-Purpose Division
articles.summary: The Dangarian Empire’s secret service: counterintelligence and surveillance answerable directly to the Kaiser. Its officers, especially Wolf Klein, intervene twice in the fates of Red and Dietrich.

articles.title: Mergana
articles.ru: Mergana
articles.summary: A small scholarly country on the River Khursla, the philosopher van Halm’s homeland; to Catalians, the western edge of the known world, and to Dangar, a country that closed the waterway through its territory at the height of the war.

articles.title: Muari Emirates
articles.ru: Muaris, or the Muari Emirates
articles.summary: An overseas continent under one god, divided into emirates; Catalia’s trading partner and the enemy of Catalian pirates, competing with Catalia for supremacy over the Miriam Sea.

articles.title: Ollandia
articles.ru: The Grand Principality of Ollandia
articles.summary: A proud but fragmented country between Catalia and Dangar, being conquered by the Dangarian army at the start of the novel; in the author’s conception, it resembles the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

articles.title: Reformists
articles.ru: The Reformists (“Yellow Ribbons”)
articles.summary: A movement of Laerta’s obreros, masters, and students seeking changes to the High Table and protection for workers against steam-powered machines. Led by the engineer Mor, its circle includes Fernan and Lucille Gereira, the student Wasp, and the giant Little One.

articles.title: Academy of Arts
articles.ru: Academy of Arts in Laerta
articles.summary: An educational institution of the Art esfera in Laerta, where Alvaro lectures on the craft of writing.

articles.title: Bargot
articles.ru: The City of Bargot
articles.summary: The capital of Ollandia on the River Khursla; the objective of Kurtzleben’s southern army.

articles.title: Brega
articles.ru: The Province of Brega
articles.summary: The coal-producing industrial province of Catalia on the River Monho, a source of steam-powered machinery and engines.

articles.title: Chinkhar
articles.ru: Chinkhar, Land of the Chinkharians
articles.summary: A northern land conquered by Dangar during the Chinkhar Wars; its people are described as having “Chinkharian blood.”

articles.title: Dunkwald
articles.ru: The Settlement of Dunkwald
aliases: settlement of the Fishermen’s Guild’s stones
articles.summary: A forest settlement of enslaved stones belonging to the Fishermen’s Guild, where experimental wells are dug; the site of Red’s penal labor.

articles.title: Eyring
articles.ru: The City of Eyring
aliases: Ancestral seat of the von Eyrings
articles.summary: A city in Dangar, the hereditary possession of the ancient von Eyring family.

articles.title: Eliste Gallery
articles.ru: The Eliste Gallery in Laerta
articles.summary: Laerta’s celebrated art gallery, with a three-hundred-year-old collection and scandalous temporary exhibitions.

articles.title: Gerona
articles.ru: The City of Gerona
articles.summary: A city in northern Catalia, known only from the author’s map.

articles.title: Ginarva
articles.ru: The City of Ginarva (Girnava)
articles.summary: A river town in Ollandia, where the railway from Catalia ends and steamship travel along the Khursla begins.

articles.title: Grand Opera
articles.ru: The Grand Opera Theater in Laerta
articles.summary: Laerta’s principal opera house, where Don Filippe di Berro sings and “Señorita Violet” is staged.

articles.title: Indra
articles.ru: Indra Fortress
articles.summary: A Catalian border fortress on the route to Ollandia, the final stop before the frontier.

articles.title: Hofstadt
articles.ru: Hofstadt, Capital of Dangar
articles.summary: The capital of the Dangarian Empire on the River Wunde, a city of two million people where Dietrich von Dort’s family lives.

articles.title: Khursla
articles.ru: The River Khursla
articles.summary: Ollandia’s largest navigable river, flowing through Mergana into the Kobold Sea.

articles.title: Mercy Clinic
articles.ru: Mercy Clinic, a Hospital for the Mentally Ill
articles.summary: A Catalian hospital for the mentally ill, where Dr. Juanes placed the deranged philosopher Liess van Halm. Its orderlies charge for visits and for “entertainments.”

articles.title: Laerta
articles.ru: Laerta, Capital of Catalia
articles.summary: The capital of Catalia, a city of eleven esfera districts, where Alvaro da Silva lives and works and the country’s most important disputes are settled.

articles.title: Latsen
articles.ru: The City of Latsen
articles.summary: A city in central Ollandia, occupied by the Dangarian army; Field Marshal Reiniger’s headquarters.

articles.title: Mershants
articles.ru: Mershants Fortress
articles.summary: A powerful Ollandian fortress on the eastern frontier, close to Catalia’s border, besieged by Hofmeyer’s army.

articles.title: Ortiyar Fortress
articles.ru: Ortiyar, the Fortress and Railway Junction Known as the “Shield of Laerta”
articles.summary: A railway junction and system of fortifications thirty miles from Laerta, where General Deserey serves.

articles.title: Chamber of the Word
articles.ru: The Chamber of the Word in Laerta
articles.summary: The building in Laerta where dueling debates are held and bracelets awarded; the heart of Catalian justice.

articles.title: Plyutva
articles.ru: The City of Plyutva
articles.summary: The first major Ollandian city in the path of the Dangarian invasion, captured and almost destroyed by artillery.

articles.title: Last Winter
articles.ru: Last Winter Castle (the House Above)
articles.summary: A ruined feudal castle above Tres Molinos, where the philosopher van Halm lived and a dark schönbrun lies hidden.

articles.title: Selezia
articles.ru: The Province of Selezia
articles.summary: A rice-growing province of Catalia, with mountains, ruins, and “dreary ballads,” where the philosopher van Halm settles.

articles.title: Solanta
articles.ru: The Island of Solanta
articles.summary: A small island amid reefs and currents, where Catalian heroes performed a great feat sixteen years ago and a treaty with Catalia was subsequently signed.

articles.title: Old Port
articles.ru: The Old Port of Laerta
articles.summary: The “black” port district of Laerta, where pirates, assassins, and smugglers operate and the law barely intervenes.

articles.title: Tres Molinos
articles.ru: The Little Town of Tres Molinos
articles.summary: A tiny town in a Selezian gorge, overlooked by the philosopher van Halm’s castle.

articles.title: Three Bulls
articles.ru: The Three Bulls Tavern and Inn
articles.summary: A tavern at the meeting point of the Craft, Service, and Agriculture districts in Laerta, serving as a headquarters for workers and Reformists; an alliance of esferas shares its name.

sledy-na-vode.date: Spring sunset, on the evening before ch. 1
sledy-na-vode.place: Del Toro Boulevard in Laerta
sledy-na-vode.sum: The thirty-three-year-old novelist Alvaro Flores da Silva introduces himself: four novels, a silver bracelet as a master of art, and a dream of inscribing his name on the Scroll as his grandfather Ricardo did. He walks through Laerta at sunset with Fernan and Lucille Gereira, who outline their political reforms. Alvaro announces that from here on he will speak of himself in the third person.

sledy-na-vode.date: Spring; evening and the next day at 3 p.m.
sledy-na-vode.place: A restaurant by the Grand Opera; the Chamber of the Word
sledy-na-vode.sum: At an expensive restaurant, master of law Vincente Ramires da Rimini calls Fernan and Lucille obreros unworthy of the place. Alvaro challenges him to a duel; Ramires proposes a duel debate. Alvaro loses at the Chamber of the Word the next day and must pay seven thousand escudos.

sledy-na-vode.date: Autumn; about a month after Plyutva falls
sledy-na-vode.place: A bare hill near a railway halt and the ruins of a farm behind the lines in Ollandia
sledy-na-vode.sum: Lieutenant Dietrich von Dort inspects the enslaved “stones” of a Dangarian battery and speaks with the blessed man Salvation and Neubiy. The stones flee at night after maiming Corporal Gelb. Ollandian hussars attack in the morning. After looking into the well, Dietrich takes command when Staff Captain Zeidvist dies, defeats the hussars with three volleys of grapeshot, and kills Salvation.

sledy-na-vode.date: Within three days of losing the debate; day and evening
sledy-na-vode.place: The Academy of Arts, a bank, and the Grand Opera in Laerta
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro lectures on protagonists, meets the blond reformist Wasp, and learns he has only 4,600 escudos. Backstage at Señorita Violet, Don Filippe di Berro commissions a book on four (later five) heroes of the Solantian Expedition and offers to cover the debt and pay another three thousand.

sledy-na-vode.date: Late autumn and first snow; nine months into the year the doctor gave Red
sledy-na-vode.place: An enslaved settlement deep in Dangar and Joriksen’s house
sledy-na-vode.sum: The narrator follows the rail line from Catalia through Ollandia and Mergana into Dangar, where the third protagonist, Red, is enslaved. He stands up to the foreman, digs what he thinks is his grave, and learns from Fritjof Joriksen that a well could earn him his freedom. Terminally ill, Red demands that his letter be sent to Laerta first.

sledy-na-vode.h: A Corpse Is a Wonderful Thing!
sledy-na-vode.date: The day after ch. 3; evening, then morning and a lecture at three
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta: the Three Bulls tavern, Juanes’s house, and the Academy
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro tells his friends about Filippe’s commission; Fernan volunteers as his secretary. They question Emil and the widow at the home of the recently deceased doctor Garcia Juanes. Alvaro pockets an anonymous note and discusses the death in a lecture on plot openings.

sledy-na-vode.date: A day or two after the battle at the halt; Latsen fell three months ago
sledy-na-vode.place: Latsen: a summer restaurant in the square, then the town hall
sledy-na-vode.sum: Dietrich, recommended for promotion, meets the Ollandian Olkha at a restaurant. Major Wolfgang von Klein tells him he is suspected of treason. Unable to mention the well, his chief defense, Dietrich is suspended and ordered to wait in Hofstadt.

sledy-na-vode.date: Daytime, after the obreros’ debate with factory owners at the Chamber of the Word
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta: the waterfront, Old Port, and Carlos el Niña’s fort
sledy-na-vode.sum: Fernan tries to show Alvaro the world’s injustices, but Alvaro takes him to the smuggler Carlos el Niña, the first subject of the book. They endure a cruel pistol prank and meet the ailing Doña Isabel. In the cellar Carlos shows them a newly unearthed well with a giant chrysanthemum, entwined in a vine, wilting at its bottom.

sledy-na-vode.date: Winter; the first weeks of captivity, with the pit a yard and a half deep
sledy-na-vode.place: Joriksen’s enslaved settlement: the crew’s dugout, a clearing, and a wooden church
sledy-na-vode.sum: Red digs the well and endures abuse from the foreman and his men. At a service where free people feed porridge to enslaved people, he refuses food from another’s hand and catches the Black Falcon’s eye. After a beating in the forest, he takes on the crew and establishes an equal division of food.

sledy-na-vode.date: The morning after visiting Carlos, then the day’s journey and the night
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta, Ortiyar Fortress fortress, and a roadside inn
sledy-na-vode.sum: Beatriz drives Alvaro and Fernan to General Deserey at Ortiyar Fortress. He critiques Alvaro’s battle scenes, demonstrates grapeshot, and asks him to make fear of Dangar the book’s theme. On the way back Alvaro realizes Deserey lied about his last visit to Juanes; a green steam carriage follows them.

sledy-na-vode.date: Late summer, in Gehai; a month’s journey after dismissal
sledy-na-vode.place: Hofstadt: the Witwen district and the von Dorts’ apartment
sledy-na-vode.sum: Dietrich returns to his wife Marie and son Heinz. His letter never reached Marie, and they are nearly out of money. After a fruitless job search and an argument, he gives most of their savings to Frau Gizeke for a ticket to Baroness Walbrecht’s fishing.

sledy-na-vode.date: The day after the journey to Ortiyar
sledy-na-vode.place: An inn on the road from Ortiyar Fortress; Laerta: the servants’ district, the station, and Foucault Street
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro and Fernan mistake chauffeur Hugo Martines for a spy. Alvaro drives Beatriz away by writing to her father. In Laerta he witnesses a protest of dismissed obreros dispersed with blank cannon fire and comes home to a gruesome gift in his notebook.

sledy-na-vode.date: Winter; several months later, with the well twelve to thirteen yards deep
sledy-na-vode.place: Joriksen’s settlement: the dugout, the church, the women’s farm, and the forest
sledy-na-vode.sum: Red reaches water and expects to be freed the next day. Instead, Yakka takes him to the women’s farm for a night with Greta. Realizing this is his reward in place of freedom, Red strikes Yakka, takes his gun, and flees.

sledy-na-vode.date: Several days after finding the finger; a three-day drinking bout
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta: the Arts district, the factory district, and Maduro’s estate
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro gives a listless lecture on flawed protagonists. Constable Ingres tells him the severed finger in his desk is no grounds for a suit. He writes to Filippe to give up the book. Fernan makes him visit Maduro, where Salvador questions him and Alvaro outlines his own plan to reform the Esfera of Production.

sledy-na-vode.date: Summer; the day of the fishing, the last day of Gehai
sledy-na-vode.place: Hofstadt: Baroness Walbrecht’s mansion and its schönbrun; the von Dort home
sledy-na-vode.sum: Dietrich secretly spends 200 marks from the family’s stash on the fishing, run by Fritjof Joriksen at the baroness’s schönbrun. He sees Olkha with her uncle Prince Lenz, tells Joriksen about his own schönbrun, and receives an invitation. He confesses to Marie that evening.

sledy-na-vode.date: Winter; a few days after the escape
sledy-na-vode.place: The enslaved settlement: dugouts, the women’s farm, and the gravestone
sledy-na-vode.sum: Yakka tracks a freezing Red and brings him back. Baron Landau wants to execute him, but Joriksen explains that Red must dig a schönbrun. Red is given a dugout of his own and works at night by a fire. He sings Catalian songs, Greta carries his letter home, and he realizes Joriksen has recreated Catalian surroundings for him.

sledy-na-vode.date: The day of the exhibition; the stranger arranges a meeting for 7 p.m. two days later
sledy-na-vode.place: The Eliste Gallery and Jose Flarbo’s bookshop in Laerta
sledy-na-vode.sum: Filippe calls Alvaro to the Philosophy of Horror exhibition, demands that he write the book, and shows him a newspaper item about a fight at the station. At Flarbo’s shop Alvaro learns the story of the deranged philosopher van Halm and arranges to meet a clever stranger.

sledy-na-vode.date: Saturday at five in the afternoon and that evening; autumn
sledy-na-vode.place: Hofstadt: the Astoria hotel, Count von Lourd’s house in Schlüssel, and Witwenplatz
sledy-na-vode.sum: At Olkha’s request, Dietrich poses as a cousin of her friend Katrina von Eyring, Count Ludwig von Lourd’s wife. Over dinner the count explains world politics and the situation in Dangar. The evening ends in a kiss in the carriage and an argument at home: Marie refuses to let him in.

sledy-na-vode.date: The morning after the meeting at the shop, then the day and evening
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta: the Old Port and Carlos el Niña’s fort
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro asks Carlos about Juanes’s death and finds him distraught over Doña Isabel’s disappearance. After a reckless revolver game, the friends get drunk. Alvaro hears about the sailor da Vira and learns that Juanes talked too much. On the way back a stranger shoots Alvaro through the palm and tells him not to write.

sledy-na-vode.date: Winter thaw; from the third yard of the dig to the water
sledy-na-vode.place: The enslaved settlement and surrounding forest in Dangar
sledy-na-vode.sum: Red notices he is being watched and that his letter has gone missing; it is then returned. Landau shows him a camp where hundreds of enslaved people dig in vain for wells. Red reaches water in the thaw and realizes his cough is gone, but the foreman buries him in the pit.

sledy-na-vode.date: The night and day after Alvaro is shot
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta: the Old Port and Three Bulls tavern
sledy-na-vode.sum: Friends tend to Alvaro at the Three Bulls. Mor, chief engineer at Esperanza, explains the reformists’ aims and asks him to influence Allen Fatima. Feeling used, Alvaro storms out. Beatriz picks him up; they reconcile, and he takes her on as a student and assistant.

sledy-na-vode.date: The morning after the visit to the Lourds in ch. 17; by three o’clock
sledy-na-vode.place: Hofstadt: Frau Gizeke’s apartment, Joriksen’s mansion, and the hotel
sledy-na-vode.sum: Sober again and short of money and land, Dietrich goes to Joriksen, who demands Heinz as collateral. Dietrich leaves, finds Prince Lenz listed in the guild’s atlas as owner of the land with the schönbrun, and returns with a different contract.

sledy-na-vode.date: The day before Alvaro’s lecture; six months before the election for supremo
sledy-na-vode.place: The road out of Laerta and back; the Great Scroll
sledy-na-vode.sum: Driving an Esperanza car, Alvaro and Beatriz theorize that their adversaries are a Dangarian spy and Fatima’s aggrieved son. In the Scroll’s archive Alvaro pieces together the story of Rodrigo da Vira and Carmencita Estevos, but Beatriz finds only a daughter of Fatima named Unoco.

sledy-na-vode.date: Spring; just after the well collapses, followed by about a month of recovery
sledy-na-vode.place: Dunkwald and the women’s settlement of Katzen
sledy-na-vode.sum: Lieutenant Klein argues with Baron Landau, who demonstrates the power of an oberfischmeister. Red recovers in Greta’s home, debates the Sower with an enslaved temple servant, and digs out the well again on the baron’s orders. When he reaches water, Landau declares that it is no schönbrun.

sledy-na-vode.date: The evening of the second meeting with the stranger and the next day
sledy-na-vode.place: The hospital’s anatomy theater, Juanes’s house, and Laerta
sledy-na-vode.sum: The stranger takes Alvaro to an autopsy. He flees the theater but realizes how Doctor Juanes died. The following day he and Beatriz establish that Emil gave the doctor the wrong medicine. Beatriz gets him to talk about van Halm, who saw the heroes of Solanta in the well.

sledy-na-vode.h: Allow Me to Propose a Solution
sledy-na-vode.date: Autumn; ten days before the train leaves for Ollandia
sledy-na-vode.place: Dietrich’s hotel and Baroness Walbrecht’s mansion in Hofstadt
sledy-na-vode.sum: Dietrich keeps the mortgage details from Marie, misses Olkha, and turns up uninvited at the baroness’s. In Olkha’s bedroom Katrina stages a scene. Prince Lenz demands a duel, and Count von Lourd offers a “solution.”

sledy-na-vode.date: The day after the autopsy and the discovery about Emil; a meeting at 10 p.m.
sledy-na-vode.place: The Mercy Clinic and a passage to a wine cellar on North Rampart Street in Laerta
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro and Beatriz visit the deranged van Halm, who recognizes the names of the Solanta heroes and fears Eliga. That evening the stranger explains the election to Alvaro in a secret cellar. She takes revenge for the autopsy that night, then comes back for him.

sledy-na-vode.date: Spring; at night, a month after the cave-in
sledy-na-vode.place: Dunkwald: a dugout used as a cell, the forest, the road, and the gravestone
sledy-na-vode.sum: Klein tells the captive Red that the well was ordinary and that Joriksen devised the scheme and left. Red cuts his bonds with Klein’s knife, kills the escort, sacks the convoy, and lets a young clerk go. At the gravestone, Baron Landau stops him with his power.

sledy-na-vode.date: The morning after the night with the stranger; six months after Ollandia capitulates
sledy-na-vode.place: Fatima’s house in Laerta
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro overhears the stranger with General Deserey. She is Fatima Ir-Reya, chief allen of Law, and the general wants her to secure mobilization. Alvaro accuses her of deceiving him and quarrels with her and then with her daughter Beatriz, who concealed their relationship.

sledy-na-vode.date: The night and morning after the scandal; Dunkwald fell that spring
sledy-na-vode.place: Hofstadt: Baroness Walbrecht’s house, Witwenplatz, and the station
sledy-na-vode.sum: Count von Lourd settles the scandal with Prince Lenz by threatening to label him unsicher and proposing that Olkha marry Dietrich. Dietrich says goodbye to Marie and leaves for Ollandia with Joriksen. On the train, guild magnus Amir the Grey announces that everyone in Dunkwald died.

sledy-na-vode.date: Autumn, soon after the quarrels with Mor and Fatima; train at night
sledy-na-vode.place: Laerta: Crafts Square, general headquarters, and the Three Bulls; train to Selezia
sledy-na-vode.sum: A reproachful letter from Mor tells Alvaro that Fernan spoke to her about Beatriz. He hits Fernan, then makes peace. Alvaro gets a thousand escudos from Deserey on the pretext of tracking a spy. He tells Fernan that van Halm may have seen the Solanta heroes in a well in Selezia, and they set out.

sledy-na-vode.date: Several days in late summer or early autumn
sledy-na-vode.place: Latsen: Field Marshal Reiniger’s headquarters and the halt with the schönbrun
sledy-na-vode.sum: Major Klein learns that the field marshal is halving Hofmeyer’s army and hints that he should delay the courier. Klein sends Joriksen to study the dark schönbrun and arrests Dietrich, but releases him under pressure from Katrina and Olkha.

sledy-na-vode.date: Three days, starting the morning after the train from Laerta
sledy-na-vode.place: Tres Molinos in Selezia: the House Above, an inn, and a tavern
sledy-na-vode.sum: Alvaro and Fernan inspect the cursed House Above, where van Halm lost his mind. They learn he housed six Dangarian “servants.” Alvaro finds Isabel el Niña alive in town and demands the truth about Rodrigo da Vira.

sledy-na-vode.date: Several years, from the first execution to the spring of roughly the seventh year
sledy-na-vode.place: The beast’s pit near Dunkwald
sledy-na-vode.sum: Chained in the pit, Red becomes the condemned prisoners’ executioner under Landau’s Zustand. Years pass, Yakka and Klein leave, and Greta admits she betrayed Red before being sent to the pit herself. She is found dead the next morning. Army levy officers take Red on the recommendation of the Kaiser’s Claws.

sledy-na-vode.date: The evening of Fernan and Alvaro’s argument; Juanes is already dead
sledy-na-vode.place: Tres Molinos: Last Winter castle and the cellar with the schönbrun
sledy-na-vode.sum: At van Halm’s castle, Alvaro solves the mystery of the cursed door. Salvador and the second killer capture him, Fernan, and Beatriz. In the cellar by the dark schönbrun, Salvador is killed and the other murderer is wounded and captured. Fatima arrives and tells what happened between the heroes of Solanta.

houses.government: Union of self-governing esferas; the High Table (three allens per esfera) and an elected supremo
houses.army: Fifteen combat-ready divisions, Ortiyar Fortress fortress, rifled carbines and howitzers
houses.ending: Mobilization is debated without a decision; reformists strike; the election of a supremo is still ahead
houses.society: Esferas, bracelets, obreros, and duel debates; no taxes or duties
houses.notes: Spanish flavor, “but not Spain”; materialists, mirns rather than gods, and steam technology

houses.government: The Kaiser, the patriarch and the magnus of the fishermen’s guild; the Kaiser’s Claws
houses.army: Eagles as officers and stones as rank and file; flintlocks and mortars; supplied by rail
houses.ending: Occupies central Ollandia; Hofmeyer is near Mershants; Dunkwald is destroyed
houses.society: Eagles, hares, and enslaved stones; faith in the Sower and the feeding rite
houses.notes: German flavor, “not Prussia”; airships, marks, and the Chinhar Wars

houses.government: A grand principality of princes and voivodeships, effectively under Dangarian occupation
houses.army: Hussars and the princes’ retinues with no unified command; two Catalian howitzers near Mershants
houses.ending: The center is occupied by Dangar; the north resists; the south and Mershants await assault
houses.society: Nobles, bourgeoisie, and peasants; no slavery; pride without industry
houses.notes: Resembles the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; Slavic names; all locomotives are Catalian

houses.government: A state that acts through protests and prohibitions in the novel
houses.ending: Blocks Dangarian steamships on the Khursla; takes no part in the fighting
houses.society: Scholars and a university; white chocolate and valissian
houses.notes: Home of van Halm; the western edge of the world for Laertans

houses.capital: Unnamed; the supreme ruler is the sultan
houses.government: Emirates united by one faith and a sultan; they unite when necessary
houses.army: Galleys; sea power was lost on the Sea of Miriam
houses.ending: Does not take part; Catalia’s trading partner and a possible refuge for emigrants
houses.society: Monotheism; slavery is forbidden; harems and silk trading
houses.notes: Religious enemies of Dangar; the sorcerer Faid Musa; former ally of Solanta

events.label: About 16 years before the novel
events.t: The channel chart: Carlos el Niña buys a chart of the approach to Solanta from a Black sailor and plans the expedition with Maduro.

events.label: About 16 years before the novel
events.t: The Solantian Expedition: the schooner Santa Eliza takes a coastal fort in Solanta, and the doge signs a treaty of alliance.

events.label: About 16 years before the novel
events.t: The navigator is handed over: the doge demands the man who knows the channel. Carlos hands over Rodrigo da Vira, whom the doge sells into slavery.

events.label: Three months later
events.t: A posthumous decoration: Carlos and Fatima win their case against the High Table, and the supposedly dead navigator da Vira is awarded the Order of Courage.

events.label: Later
events.t: Carmencita Estevos’s lawsuit: the obrera Shadow asks the court to recognize her as da Vira’s widow and her infant as his son. The court refuses.

events.label: Ch. 4
events.t: A Catalian in the mycelium: Red is brought in bonds to the forest camp of enslaved diggers. Joriksen promises freedom in return for a schönbrun.

events.label: Ch. 12
events.t: A prize instead of freedom: water appears at the thirteenth yard, but Red is taken to Greta instead, and he flees into the forest.

events.label: Ch. 15
events.t: The schönbrun recipe: Yakka brings back the fugitive; the letter goes to Laerta, and Red sings as he digs at night.

events.label: Ch. 19
events.t: Buried alive: Red’s cough goes away, and the foreman buries him in the pit.

events.label: Ch. 23
events.t: No sarcoma: Baron Landau declares that the schönbrun has cured Red.

events.label: Ch. 27
events.t: Täuschung: Klein reveals the deception, Red slaughters people on the road, and Landau seizes him with an unknown power.

events.label: Ch. 33
events.t: A beast in the pit: years of executions under the Zustand, the “THOU SHALT NOT KILL” brand, and Greta’s death. Red is taken into the army.

events.label: Ch. 2–34
events.t: The Ollandian War.

events.label: Before ch. 2
events.t: Neubiy: in the army, Red becomes a “stone” rifleman in a platoon attached to Dietrich’s battery.

events.label: Ch. 2
events.t: The battle at the well on the hill.

events.label: Spring
events.t: The destruction of Dunkwald.

events.label: Ch. 14
events.t: Fishing at Baroness Walbrecht’s.

events.label: Ch. 31
events.t: Dietrich’s arrest: Klein finds a body in the well by the railway halt but backs down before the Lourds and the Eyrings.

events.label: Six months before ch. 28
events.t: Ollandia capitulates: the war is over.

events.label: Before ch. 1
events.t: Six Dangarians: van Halm hires servants from the Empire. The eldest speaks Catalian well and has letters branded below his collarbone.

events.label: Before ch. 1
